Description: Minimum valid fundamental frequency detected in the recording. F0 represents the rate of vocal-fold vibration during voiced speech.
Maximum valid fundamental frequency detected in the recording.
Arithmetic average of valid F0 measurements across the analyzed frames.
Standard deviation of F0 measurements which describes how much pitch varies around its mean.
Middle value of the valid F0 measurements after sorting and  less sensitive to extreme values than the mean.
Difference between maximum and minimum F0: F0max – F0min
Zero-crossing rate: how frequently the waveform changes sign. In libraries such as librosa, it is expressed as the fraction of zero crossings within a frame.
Unit: Dimensionless fraction crossings if explicitly time-normalized

Description: Signal strength calculated from squared sample amplitudes, commonly as a sum or mean over a frame. Check whether your code instead calculates RMS amplitude or logarithmic energy.
Unit: Squared-amplitude units for energy.  Amplitude units for RMS.  dB for a defined logarithmic measure.

Description: Likely cepstral peak prominence calculated with voice detection, restricting analysis to selected voice-active segments. CPP measures the height of the cepstral peak above its background trend.
Likely CPP calculated without voice detection, potentially including unvoiced or silent frames in the analysis. Its value therefore depends on the analyzed speech segments and calculation settings.
Possibly the F0 estimated from the cepstral peak during voice-detected segments. Cepstral F0 is obtained from the inverse of the peak’s quefrency.
First reported mel-frequency cepstral coefficient. MFCCs summarize the shape of the log-mel spectrum.In this experiment, it corresponds to coefficient c0.
Unit: No fixed physical unit.  conventionally treated as dimensionless

Description: These are the coefficient components describing the spectral envelope.
Central frequency of vocal tract resonances.
